channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Anthropic to Shift Some Shares Into New ‘Public Good’ Fund
item.description: Anthropic PBC said it plans to put 5% of its shares into a new so-called public benefit fund that allows it to make donations that can address “the public good,” including mitigating AI’s impact on the job market.
item.dc:creator: Katrina Manson

item.title: Inside Andreessen’s Growing Political Influence
item.description: Bloomberg Businessweek features writer Austin Carr tells Bloomberg This Weekend how Andreessen Horowitz co-founder Marc Andreessen became an increasingly influential Republican donor and adviser after years of shifting political allegiances, with disputes over AI, crypto and other Biden-era policies playing a role in his latest turn. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Carr explains how Andreessen has translated his Silicon Valley influence into Washington access while maintaining a political style that associates describe as more calculated than his combative online persona. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple HomeView With Robotic Arm; New Mac, iPad Mini Nov. 6 Release; iPhone Duo
item.description: Also: The company is planning Nov. 6 retail store reset, indicating potential Mac release date.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: OpenAI Arrest Raises AI Espionage Concerns
item.description: Morgan Meaker, a senior writer for Bloomberg Weekend, tells Bloomberg This Weekend about the arrest of an OpenAI engineer accused of planting a covert recording device in an executive conference room, a case highlighting growing concerns about protecting sensitive AI technology. Meaker also explains to hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini how AI training work is shifting toward highly skilled experts and why that evolution could eventually reshape the professions providing that expertise. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Short of Time and Influence, Macron Fights to Remain Relevant
item.description: Emmanuel Macron still has plenty of ideas, but in the home stretch of his presidency he’s lost much of the power to turn them into reality.
item.dc:creator: Ania Nussbaum

item.title: Nscale Says Microsoft Has Withdrawn From UK Data Center Deal
item.description: Microsoft Corp. has pulled out of a UK data center deal with Nscale, the British neocloud firm said, marking a setback for the startup’s initial public offering hopes.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Solon

item.title: PBOC Deputy Urges Private Role in Sovereign Debt Restructuring
item.description: China’s deputy central bank governor Xuan Changneng called for greater private-sector participation in sovereign debt restructuring as rising borrowing costs add to developing countries’ debt-servicing burdens.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Woodside Pauses Scarborough Pre-Commissioning Due to Protest
item.description: Woodside Energy Group Ltd. said that pre-commissioning work at its Scarborough project off the coast of Western Australia was paused after Greenpeace protesters climbed aboard the gas platform.
item.dc:creator: Brett Miller

item.title: AI Trade Reversal Pierces Asia’s Star Picks-and-Shovels Stocks
item.description: A deepening selloff in US technology stocks is exposing a new vulnerability in Asia’s artificial intelligence trade: mounting financing costs could choke off the spending needed to sustain the boom, threatening earnings across a supply chain that has powered the region’s stock-market rally.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Vishnoi, Charlotte Yang and Faseeh Mangi

item.title: Zelenskyy Says Starlink Speed Restrictions Look Deliberate
item.description: Restrictions on Ukraine’s military use of SpaceX’s Starlink system appear to be deliberate and not the result of any technical problems, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, while denouncing a US decision to waive sanctions against Russia.
item.dc:creator: Olesia Safronova and Daryna Krasnolutska
